body: NIST DLMF section 24.17 (Mathematical Applications) says: "See § 2.10(i) . For a generalization see Olver ( 1997b , p. 284) . Let 0\leq h\leq 1 and a,m , and n be integers such that n>a , m>0 , and f^{(m)}(x) is absolutely integrable over [a,n] . Then with the notation of § 24.2(iii) See Milne-Thomson ( 1933 ) , Nörlund ( 1924 ) , or Jordan ( 1965 ) . For a more modern perspective see Graham et al. ( 1994 ) . Let \mathcal{S}_{n} denote the class of functions that have n-1 continuous derivatives on \mathbb{R} and are polynomials of degree at most n in each interval (k,k+1) , k\in\mathbb{Z} . The members of \mathcal{S}_{n} are called cardinal spline functions . The functions are called Euler splines of degree n . For each n , S_{n}(x) is the unique bounded function such that S_{n}(x)\in\mathcal{S}_{n} and The function S_{n}(x) is also optimal in a certain sense; see Schoenberg ( 1971 ) . A function of the form x^{n}-S(x) , with S(x)\in\mathcal{S}_{n-1} is called a cardinal monospline of degree n . Again with the notation of § 24.2(iii) define" Equation 24.17.1 on the page has alt text "\sum_{j=a}^{n-1}(-1)^{j}f(j+h)=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{k=0}^{m-1}\frac{E_{k}\left(h% \right)}{k!}\left((-1)^{n-1}f^{(k)}(n)+(-1)^{a}f^{(k)}(a)\right)+R_{m}(n),". Equation 24.17.2 on the page has alt text "R_{m}(n)=\frac{1}{2(m-1)!}\int_{a}^{n}f^{(m)}(x)\widetilde{E}_{m-1}\left(h-x% \right)\,\mathrm{d}x.". This card records that section's wording and equation alt text. It does not retypeset a formula the alt text did not carry.
